tradeoffs.loses: OpenAI's best-effort reproducibility from seed=0 on the routed gpt-* and o1/o3 calls: identical prompts can now return different text (they already could, since seed is best-effort and these calls run at temperature 0.75)
tradeoffs.why: Router's /v1/responses rejects seed (measured, ROUTER.md section 5), so the runtime keeps every seeded Chat Completions request on OpenAI. Every gpt/o1/o3 call in llm.py sends seed=0, so without dropping it on the Router-bound copy none of this app's OpenAI traffic can move. The original request still carries seed on the provider-fallback path.

tradeoffs.loses: the same best-effort reproducibility on the review-ensemble sender; n>1 is NOT dropped, so an ensemble of several reviews still goes to OpenAI untouched - only its n=1 uses move to Router
tradeoffs.why: get_batch_responses_from_llm sends seed=0 on the same Chat Completions shape as get_response_from_llm, and Router rejects seed. Dropping n instead would silently shrink a 5-review ensemble to 1, so n is left alone and n>1 calls stay on the provider.
